accepted.s: With reference to Union Government deficits, which one of the following correctly represents the fiscal deficit in 2020-21 and 2026-27 (BE), respectively?
accepted.x: The fiscal deficit was 9.2% of GDP in 2020-21, the peak shown in the series, and is estimated at 4.3% in 2026-27 (BE).
accepted.tq: Split the options by the two years and match the fiscal-deficit column precisely.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The fiscal deficit of the Union Government for 2026-27 (BE) is estimated at:
accepted.x: The fiscal deficit target for 2026-27 is ₹16.96 lakh crore, equivalent to 4.3% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact quantitative target rather than relying only on the percentage.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union Government's deficit position:
1. The revenue deficit in 2024-25 (actual) was 1.7% of GDP.
2. The primary deficit in 2025-26 (RE) was 0.8% of GDP.
3. The revenue deficit in 2026-27 (BE) was estimated at 0.7% of GDP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The revenue deficit was 1.7% in 2024-25 and the primary deficit was 0.8% in 2025-26 (RE). The 0.7% figure for 2026-27 is the primary deficit, not the revenue deficit; the latter was 1.5%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely placed fiscal, revenue and primary deficit figures before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the fiscal-deficit glide path mentioned for the Union Government?
o: The fiscal deficit was to be brought below 3% by 2025-26, and thereafter kept constant.
The fiscal deficit was to be brought below 4.5% by 2025-26, and from 2026-27 it is calibrated annually to keep debt falling.
The fiscal deficit was to be eliminated by 2025-26 through reduction of capital expenditure.
The fiscal deficit was to be increased above 5% by 2025-26 to accelerate capital expenditure.
accepted.x: The commitment was to bring the fiscal deficit below 4.5% by 2025-26. The target of 4.4% was achieved, after which annual calibration is intended to keep debt falling.
accepted.tq: Use the direction and purpose of the glide path to eliminate reversed or extreme claims.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The gross fiscal deficit of the Union Government reached the earlier peak of 8.4% of GDP in:
accepted.x: The earlier gross fiscal-deficit peak was 8.4% of GDP in 1990-91.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent crisis-period years using the exact benchmark year.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Revenue deficit in FY25 was described as the lowest since:
accepted.x: Revenue deficit in FY25 was the lowest recorded since FY09.
accepted.tq: Treat the reference year as a direct year-based recall point.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At the end of July 2026, the Union fiscal deficit amounted to:
accepted.x: By July-end 2026, the fiscal deficit was ₹4,55,144 crore, representing 26.8% of the 2026-27 target; the comparable earlier-year figure was 29.9%.
accepted.tq: Match the amount with its percentage and reject the swapped year-on-year comparison.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The estimated Debt-GDP ratio for 2026-27 (BE), compared with the revised estimate for 2025-26, is:
accepted.x: The Debt-GDP ratio is estimated at 55.6% in 2026-27 (BE), lower than 56.1% in 2025-26 (RE).
accepted.tq: Check the direction of change as well as the two numerical values.
accepted.sec: Deficit trends - latest Union deficits, glide path, historical peaks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: In a deficit budget, expenditure exceeds receipts. In a balanced budget receipts equal expenditure, while in a surplus budget receipts exceed expenditure.
accepted.tq: Start from the defining equality or inequality in each budget type.
accepted.sec: Budget types  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A budget in which each item of expenditure is justified afresh from zero in every period is called:
accepted.x: Zero-based budgeting requires every expenditure item to be justified afresh from zero for each period.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official term from its defining procedure.
accepted.sec: Budget types  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Zero-based budgeting was devised by Peter Pyhrr and first used in government by:
accepted.x: Peter Pyhrr devised zero-based budgeting, and Jimmy Carter was the first to use it in government.
accepted.tq: Apply the person–contribution trap by separating the deviser from the government user.
accepted.sec: Budget types  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Performance budgeting links spending to activities or work done.
2. Outcome budgeting links outlays to measurable outcomes.
3. Gender budgeting views allocations by their gender impact.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe performance, outcome and gender budgeting respectively.
accepted.tq: Test each budget type against its defining linkage before accepting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Budget types  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding specialised budget practices in India is correct?
o: Zero-based budgeting links outlays only to gender impact.
Outcome budgeting was introduced in India only after 2020.
Performance budgeting began in India from 2005-06 on the advice of the Finance Commission.
Output-Outcome budgeting began from 2005-06, while the Gender Budget Statement has also been presented since 2005-06.
accepted.x: Output-Outcome budgeting and the Gender Budget Statement are associated with 2005-06. Performance budgeting in India dates from the late 1960s on ARC advice.
accepted.tq: Separate similar budget labels by their starting period and distinctive purpose.
accepted.sec: Budget types  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 16th Finance Commission has associated Centrally Sponsored Schemes with:
o: Fixed non-plan expenditure without performance conditions
accepted.x: The 16th Finance Commission has pushed output-based spending by linking Centrally Sponsored Schemes to measurable outcomes.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with the specific reform objective rather than a broad fiscal slogan.
accepted.sec: Budget types  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Capital expenditure is expenditure that generally:
o: Never includes loans given by the government
Is limited to payment of interest
accepted.x: Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities; examples include capital works, loans given and debt repayment.
accepted.tq: Apply the core classification rule rather than memorising isolated examples.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The distinction between Plan and non-Plan expenditure in the Union Budget was scrapped from:
accepted.x: The old Plan and non-Plan classification, linked to Five-Year Plans, was scrapped from Budget 2017-18.
accepted.tq: Use the adjacent-year options to test the precise transition point.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Developmental expenditure primarily relates to:
o: Debt charges and court decrees בלבד
accepted.x: Developmental expenditure covers economic and social services, whereas interest, defence, administration and pensions are classified as non-developmental.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the developmental service group and the non-developmental group.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about charged expenditure:
1. It is not submitted to vote in the Lok Sabha.
2. It may be discussed in Parliament.
3. It is charged directly on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Charged expenditure is not voted upon, though it can be discussed, and it is drawn directly from the Consolidated Fund.
accepted.tq: Separate the ideas of voting, discussion and withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the charged items specified under Article 112(3)?
o: Salaries of all Members of Parliament
Salary and pension of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
Salaries and pensions of Supreme Court judges
Debt charges of the Government of India
accepted.x: Article 112(3) includes debt charges, specified judicial salaries and pensions, and the salary and pension of the CAG, among other items. Salaries of all Members of Parliament are not listed as a charged item in the material.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the constitutional list instead of choosing a familiar charged expense.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following constitutional provisions is correctly matched?
o: Article 112(3) — No withdrawal except under an Appropriation Act
accepted.x: Article 266 concerns the Consolidated Fund. Article 112(3) lists charged expenditure, while Article 114(3) requires an Appropriation Act for withdrawal.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number trap by matching each provision with its exact subject.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The guiding rule that borrowings should be used only to invest and not to fund current spending is most closely related to:
o: Using borrowed resources for productive capital formation
Using only tax revenue for infrastructure
Financing recurrent revenue expenditure through debt
Replacing all capital expenditure with subsidies
accepted.x: The guiding fiscal rule is to borrow for investment or productive capital formation rather than for current expenditure.
accepted.tq: Apply the fiscal principle to distinguish investment borrowing from borrowing for consumption.
accepted.sec: Expenditure classification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a major subsidy head identified for India?
accepted.x: Food, fertiliser and petroleum, including LPG, are major subsidy heads. Foreign exchange reserves are not a subsidy head.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider from the standard list of major subsidy heads.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of an explicit subsidy?
o: Implicit benefit from tax concessions בלבד
Cheap credit without a stated subsidy allocation
accepted.x: Food, fertiliser, export and interest subsidies are explicit subsidies. Under-pricing of public services and certain tax concessions or cheap credit may constitute implicit or hidden subsidies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish directly recognised subsidy heads from indirect or hidden benefits.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a hidden or implicit subsidy?
accepted.x: Under-pricing of education, health and other public services is a hidden or implicit subsidy. Tax concessions and cheap credit can also create hidden subsidies.
accepted.tq: Look for an indirect price benefit rather than an expressly budgeted subsidy.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The largest fertiliser subsidy item is:
accepted.x: Urea is the largest fertiliser subsidy item.
accepted.tq: Recall the leading item in the fertiliser-subsidy classification.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy regime, which category of fertilisers is covered?
accepted.x: P&K fertilisers are covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy regime, whereas urea is identified separately as the largest subsidy item.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the separately treated urea subsidy and the P&K category.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the national Direct Benefit Transfer system for fertiliser rolled out in 2018, subsidy is released to companies after:
o: Retail sale is recorded through PoS machines with Aadhaar authentication of the buyer
The State Legislature approves each individual transaction
The fertiliser is manufactured, without any retail verification
The buyer submits a post-purchase paper claim to the Finance Ministry
accepted.x: Under fertiliser DBT, retail sale is recorded on PoS machines and the buyer is authenticated through Aadhaar; the subsidy is then released to the companies.
accepted.tq: Follow the transaction sequence and identify the point at which the subsidy is released.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding subsidies:
1. Tax concessions can constitute hidden subsidies.
2. Cheap credit can constitute hidden subsidies.
3. Fertiliser subsidies are confined exclusively to P&K fertilisers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Tax concessions and cheap credit can be hidden subsidies. Statement 3 is false because urea is also a major fertiliser subsidy item, while P&K fertilisers are under the Nutrient Based Subsidy regime.
accepted.tq: Reject the exclusive claim after checking the separate treatment of urea and P&K fertilisers.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Major subsidies in the first quarter of FY27 rose by approximately:
accepted.x: Major subsidies rose by 37.4% in Q1 of FY27, associated with a spike in crude oil prices following developments in West Asia.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage and avoid shifting the leading digit in a quantitative option.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The rise in major subsidies in Q1 FY27 was principally associated with:
o: A fall in crude oil prices
A complete withdrawal of LPG subsidies
A spike in crude oil prices linked to West Asia
A reduction in fertiliser prices due to excess supply
accepted.x: The increase was attributed to a spike in crude oil prices associated with developments in West Asia.
accepted.tq: Match the fiscal effect with its stated external price shock, not with a reversed trend.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Major subsidies may overshoot the budget estimate by approximately:
accepted.x: Major subsidies were expected to overshoot the budget by about ₹50,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Identify the approximate fiscal overrun from the ascending amount options.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 16th Finance Commission has called for:
o: Expansion of hidden subsidies without budgetary disclosure
Replacing all subsidies with defence expenditure
accepted.x: The 16th Finance Commission has asked for rationalisation of subsidies rather than their complete abolition.
accepted.tq: Distinguish rationalisation from the stronger and unsupported claim of complete abolition.
accepted.sec: Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
